newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian cargo craft brings supplies to Mir station.
newsitem.headline: Russian cargo craft brings supplies to Mir station.

text.p: A Russian cargo craft docked with the Mir space station on Friday, bringing much-needed supplies to the two Russian cosmonauts and U.S. astronaut who have been in orbit for two months.
A mission control spokesman said the freighter linked up with Mir at 4.01 a.m. (0101 GMT).
"The docking has passed successfully in automatic mode. The Mir crew plans to open the door at 5.33 a.m (0233 GMT)," the spokesman told Reuters.

Speaking by telephone from the control centre, located in Kaliningrad near Moscow, he said the Mir crew -- cosmonauts Valery Korzun and Alexander Koleri and U.S. astronaut John Blaha -- woke up at about 1 a.m..
They would begin unloading the cargo later in the the day.

The Progress M-33 cargo craft was carrying 2.4 tonnes of food, water, fuel and equipment, including tanks and pumps to relieve one of the crew's most pressing problems -- damaged toilets on the 10-year-old space station.

The craft, launched on Tuesday from Baikonur cosmodromme in Kazakhstan, also contains Christmas and New Year gifts from the crew's families. Blaha and his two Russian colleagues have been on Mir station since September 19.
This supply mission has been delayed for over a month, mainly due to financial problems which held up production of the Soyuz-U booster rocket.
The Mir crew had been due to be relieved in mid-December. But cash problems caused the launch of the next crew, including a German, to be postponed to February.

Russia is still smarting from the embarrassing loss of its Mars-96 mission earlier this week when the unmanned Mars-96 probe crashed into the sea off Chile a day after liftoff. The probe took off two years late due to a lack of state funds.
Around $300 million worth of work and equipment was lost when the stricken craft failed to break out of Earth's orbit.
Some officials have said shortage of cash for Russia's presigious space programme was at the root of the calamity.
